{{short description|Scottish physician and academic (1721-1797)}}
{{For|the American chemist|J. Lawrence Smith (chemist)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''John Smith''' (1721–1797)<ref name="jb"/> was a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] physician and academic.<ref name="8c"/>

Smith was born in [[Maybole]], [[Scotland]], where his father, William, was a merchant.<ref name="jb">{{citation|title=James Beattie's London Diary, 1773, Issue 122|first=James|last=Beattie|publisher=The University Press|year=1946|page=131}}.</ref><ref name="snell">{{citation|title=The Snell exhibitions: From the University of Glasgow to Balliol college, Oxford|first=William Innes|last=Addison|publisher=J. MacLehose & sons|year=1901|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hgwOAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA45|page=45|isbn=9780259730767 }}.</ref>
He studied at the [[University of Glasgow]] beginning in 1736, entered [[Balliol College, Oxford]] in 1744 with the support of the [[Snell Exhibition]], and earned a B.A. in 1748 and an M.A. in 1751 from Balliol.<ref name="jb"/><ref name="snell"/>
He then studied under [[Nathan Alcock]] in [[St Mary Hall, Oxford|St Mary Hall]], earning his doctorate in 1757.<ref name="jb"/><ref name="o+c">{{citation|title=Oxford and Cambridge|first=Christopher Nugent Lawrence|last=Brooke|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=1988|isbn=9780521301398|page=241|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cq49AAAAIAAJ&pg=PA241}}.</ref> Alcock left Oxford for Bath in the same year, and Smith took his place.<ref name="o+c"/><ref name="ch@o">{{citation|title=Chemistry at Oxford: A History from 1600 to 2005|first1=Robert Joseph Paton|last1=Williams|first2=Allan|last2=Chapman|first3=John Shipley|last3=Rowlinson|publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry|year=2009|isbn=9780854041398|page=64|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=faf1nMjVRYwC&pg=PA64}}.</ref> At Oxford, he taught [[anatomy]] and [[chemistry]].<ref name="8c"/><ref name="ch@o"/> Despite not being a mathematician, he held the [[Savilian chair of geometry]] from  1766 until his death in 1797.<ref name="8c">{{citation|title=Oxford Figures: Eight Centuries of the Mathematical Sciences|first1=John|last1=Fauvel|first2=Raymond|last2=Flood|author-link2=Raymond Flood (mathematician)|first3=Robin|last3=Wilson|author-link3=Robin Wilson (mathematician)|publisher=Oxford University Press|year=2013|isbn=9780199681976|page=185|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7QexAAAAQBAJ&pg=PA185}}.</ref>
